body.heading: Build and freeze
paragraphs: Ask your adult to stand a straw in a small tub of water, with a paper triangle sail taped to it. Freeze the tub overnight.
In the morning, pop out your ice boat. The ice is the boat's body, and it floats because ice is lighter than water.

body.heading: Set sail
paragraphs: Float your boat in a big bowl of water. Blow gently behind the sail and watch it glide.
As the boat sails, it slowly melts and gets smaller. Your voyage has a time limit set by melting, which makes it extra exciting.

body.heading: Notice the melt
paragraphs: Watch the boat shrink. The sail leans more and more as the ice melts beneath it, until — plop — the boat tips over.
Icebergs are giant ice boats made by nature. They melt slowly as they drift into warmer seas, just like yours.

takeaway: An ice boat floats and sails while it melts, getting smaller until it finally tips over.
safetyNotes: An adult should prepare the frozen boat and fill the bowl. Always be with an adult around water.
screenFreeExtension: Draw the boat's journey across the bowl as a wiggly voyage map.
